without running owes nothing.

Fix saves never loading: slow-path writes to EWRAM/IWRAM were dropped

gba_wr*_slow only handled I/O, palette, VRAM, OAM and EEPROM, on the
assumption that RAM writes always take the fast path.  But the game loads
its save at boot by DMA from EEPROM into 0x0203E000, and a DMA touching a
slow region uses the slow functions on both sides, so every write was
lost and the game always saw a blank save.  Emulated unaligned stores to
RAM in TLB builds took the same path.

Found by comparing against mGBA: with a test save the game's buffer now
matches mGBA's byte for byte.

Version our UI changes as a patch, never the game's class

src/ui/<Class>.as.patch holds only our changes to a class of the game. At build time the original class is decompiled from the game's own movie (cached in work/cache), the patch is applied with git, and the full file is written to work/ui, where it is edited; every build regenerates the patch from it. Classes written entirely for the mod can still live in src/ui as .as.

The rebuilt bundle is byte-identical to the previous one, and a fresh clone regenerates the same full file. doctor checks git; .gitattributes keeps patches byte-exact.

Download missing map files from the TribesNext depot

When a server's map needs an interior, shape or terrain the client lacks,
the game disconnects with a "missing file" message. With the opt-in
net.depot_downloads option, the hook wraps the stock disconnect handler:
depot.py finds the file in the TribesNext depot index, checks its size
and MD5, and saves it under ~/.loki/tribes2/base. The game then rescans
its mod paths and rejoins, retrying while the server changes maps.

itemId1/itemId2 pair of a unit already registered. The game reuses object

real handle has; null would mean "not seen yet") and add the new unit.

that does not parse, is null with a note.

Prove decision recall for the settle-late game and state existence

The joint action into each settle-late state is determined by the state, so
each player's own play is a function of the state, and at a decision a
function of the player's view. The game therefore has decision recall and, as a
finite game, a sequential equilibrium. `settle_late_not_preserved_for_every_margin`
now states that the late game has one, so no late-leak theorem in Paper
quantifies over a possibly empty set of equilibria.

GCC's inline sqrt.s calls `sqrtf` when the result is NaN; in the game

symbol was unknown to the link, so matched C built `jal 0`. It is now a
hand symbol in config/symbol_addrs.txt (absolute:True: it is outside
every splat segment) and build.py defines such symbols for the link.

feat(multiplayer): hold a dropped player's seat and let the connection resume it (#117)

* feat(multiplayer): hold a dropped player's seat and let the connection resume it

A connection that dropped in a running game used to remove the seat at once, ending the game for everybody (or closing the room when it was the host's). The relay now holds the seat for 30 s; the client keeps its match, reconnects with backoff and sends `resume` with the seat's token. The heartbeat tolerates three missed pings, guests drop a silent connection themselves, and the relay logs why connections end.
